newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Astra surges as takeover talk resurfaces.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Astra surges as takeover talk resurfaces.

text.p: Shares in Indonesia's largest automobile manufacturer Astra International surged on Friday after a newspaper reported that a group linked to President Suharto was looking for a stake.
Brokers said rumours were rife in the market that a takeover bid was in the closing stages and added that local retailers were driving up the shares.
Astra topped the transactions list, rising 350 rupiah (15.2 U.S. cents) to 3,900 by late afternoon on a volume of 10.17 million shares on the local board.
Timber tycoon Muhamad "Bob" Hasan was quoted as saying in an interview with the Kompas newspaper that the Nusamba group he controls was interested in buying a stake in Astra for investment purposes.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan, a close associate of Suharto, and the president's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto each own 10 percent.

"We don't have any shares in Astra. But then we have an obligation to maintain the value of funds that we hold, we always look to investing it in a profitable firm," Hasan was quoted as saying in the interview. "We see that Astra International is a good and wealthy company to invest in."
A spokeswoman for Hasan said he was not immediately available for comment on the newspaper report.
The head of a foreign brokerage in Jakarta said the buying of Astra shares was all local. "The foreign stock has done very little. All the excitement is on the local board."
Astra's foreign shares were down 100 rupiah at 3,700.

But other brokers said there were strong rumours that tobacco magnate Putera Sampoerna, who effectively owns a 12.66 percent stake in Astra bought last month, had increased his holdings with purchases from state pension funds.
The brokers said that Sampoerna, who heads cigarette maker PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, could be in a position to announce a controlling interest in Astra.
A spokesman for PT Sampoerna said he had no comment.
Hasan said in the newspaper interview that some shareholders in Astra had been approached to see if they were willing to sell their stake but gave no details if any agreements had been reached.
Astra shares soared last month on newspaper reports that a takeover bid may be in progress but tapered off after Putera Sampoerna announced he had bought a 9.81 percent stake in the firm.
PT Sampoerna then announced that a subsidiary had bought an additional 2.85 percent stake.

Hasan has previously denied rumours that he is seeking to buy out Putera Sampoerna's stake but brokers said on Friday that the two could be acting in concert. There was no immediate word if Hasan's Nusamba group had actually bought any Astra shares.
Astra is a widely held company and brokers have said an 18-20 percent stake may be sufficient to gain a controlling interest.
Japan's Toyota Motor Co holds an 8.26 percent stake.
